newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Croat ex-soldier offers evidence to UN tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Croat ex-soldier offers evidence to UN tribunal.

text.p: A former Bosnian Croat soldier has told U.N. officials he is ready to offer evidence about alleged atrocities to the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia, Western officials said on Thursday.
Tribunal investigators were due to interview the soldier over the next 48 hours to decide whether his testimony implicated suspected war criminals, U.N. sources said.
The soldier contacted an international police officer on Monday in the southwestern city of Mostar, saying he feared for his security.

"He said he believed he was involved or had been a witness to war crimes," one Western official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. "We don't know what credence to give his testimony at this point," the official said.
A U.N. source in Mostar said that the soldier would be interviewed in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo. The soldier's nationality remained confidential.

A NATO raid this month against two Serbs indicted by the United Nations tribunal has fuelled a wave of speculation about who might be arrested next and who may be charged in sealed, or secret, indictments.
The soldier approached U.N. officials because "he was afraid he might be picked up," either by NATO soldiers or by Croat authorities, Western officials said.
It was not clear if the soldier had evidence against Croats already indicted by the tribunal or other potential suspects, officials said.

The former commander of the Bosnian Croat militia (HVO), General Tihomir Blaskic, is currently on trial before the tribunal in The Hague on charges connected with the "ethnic cleansing" of Moslem civilians in the central Lasva valley.
Croats and Moslems fought a 10-month war for territory during the 1992-95 Bosnian conflict before renewing their alliance against separatist Serb forces.
